english.summary: The study compares a single market maker with a desk split into a quoter and an inventory manager on Polymarket’s five-minute BTC up/down contracts. The desk performed worst when the quoter earned the spread at execution while the inventory manager absorbed subsequent inventory gains and losses. Charging the quoter for adverse post-fill price moves reduced losses, but no configuration showed a positive mean profit in periodic out-of-sample evaluation.
english.mainResult: Averaged over the last five evaluations on the held-out day, terminal portfolio value per episode was $-72.3$ ticks for the basic split. Partially sharing desk P&L improved this to $-41.0$; adding a five-step post-fill midprice markout to the quoter’s reward instead improved it to $-5.9$. A configuration combining reward sharing, a phased-in markout, a loss stop and other changes ranked first at $-4.3$. In a separate deterministic evaluation of the final policies on 48 windows, the basic split lost in 45 windows, compared with 6 for the markout variant and 8 for the combined configuration. The latter two totaled $+133$ and $+67$ ticks on those windows, respectively, which does not establish positive expected profit.
english.practicalApplication: Evaluate a quoting policy not only on the spread earned at execution, but also on whether the midprice subsequently fell after a buy or rose after a sale. Distinguish quoting from supplying executed liquidity. The single-agent redesign improved terminal value from the baseline’s $-46.1$ to $-9.6$ ticks and reduced selection of the no-quote action during training from $19.2\%$ to $4.4\%$, yet executed volume also fell, from $0.056$ to $0.032$ units per step.
english.methodology: Training used 640 Up and Down token streams from four days; 192 streams from a single day two weeks after the last training day were held out. The study inferred order messages from L2 depth changes and trade prints, then replayed each book separately through JAX-LOB’s price-time-priority engine. A learning execution agent participated in the same book in all six configurations. In the split desk, the quoter chose quotes and the inventory manager closed positions with immediate-or-cancel orders. Each trained with independent recurrent PPO. Rather than comparing their different training rewards, the study scored all configurations on terminal portfolio value after closing remaining inventory.
english.limitations: Each configuration had one training seed, and evaluation covered one day, one venue and one instrument family. Reconstructed depth matches published aggregates, but order IDs are synthetic and cancellations select orders randomly from the queue; simulated fills are not observed historical executions. Historical participants do not react to the agents’ quotes, and trading fees are omitted. The single-agent redesign jointly changes observations, actions, the forecast head and inventory controls. The best split desk changes the loss stop and forecast settings as well as the rewards. The improvements therefore cannot be attributed to individual changes, particularly the curriculum alone.
english.reason: Recommended for researchers designing rewards for electronic market making. The most informative comparison adds partial P&L sharing and post-fill markouts separately to the same split desk. Its value is as an experiment in assigning later losses to the agent whose orders created the exposure, not as evidence of a profitable live strategy.

screenAnalysis.summary: 候補回答を採点する機械学習モデルについて、教師モデルのソフトターゲット、固定表現、温度較正が予測リスクや確率の整合性に与える影響を、Gaussian surrogateと苦情データで分析しています。電子取引、マーケット・マイクロストラクチャ、金利モデル、イールドカーブを直接扱う研究ではありません。
screenAnalysis.mainResult: Gaussian surrogateでは、教師由来のバイアスは生徒データを増やしても残り、固定表現のリスク低減には標本数の閾値があると報告しています。較正は確率の尺度を修正しますが、教師の係数の向きが誤っている場合は過剰リスクを除去できません。信用カード苦情231,521件の分析では、教師確率で学習したモデルの意思決定コストは教師と同水準で、結果で学習したモデルは教師より8%低くなりました。
screenAnalysis.practicalApplication: 予測確率を意思決定に使う際、較正や事前学習表現だけに頼らず、実現した結果に照らして教師由来のバイアスを検証する必要性を示唆します。金融取引や金利業務への直接の適用は、要旨からは確認できません。
screenAnalysis.methodology: 有限標本リスクを厳密計算できるGaussian surrogateで各学習要素を分析し、probitモデルで再較正を検討しています。さらにLuce選択公理の整合条件を示し、米国消費者金融保護局の信用カード苦情データでモデルを比較しています。
screenAnalysis.limitations: 主な理論分析はGaussian surrogateに基づき、実証例は信用カード苦情の二値判断に限られます。要旨だけでは、推定の不確実性、比較設定の詳細、他のデータや業務への一般化可能性を評価できません。
screenAnalysis.reason: 機械学習モデルの較正と意思決定に関する研究で、指定された定量金融分野との直接的な関連が示されていないため、対象範囲外と判定します。

english.summary: The paper analyzes how teacher soft targets, fixed representations, and temperature calibration affect predictive risk and probability coherence in candidate-scoring models, using Gaussian surrogates and complaint data. It does not directly address electronic trading, market microstructure, interest-rate models, or yield curves.
english.mainResult: The Gaussian-surrogate analysis reports that teacher-induced bias persists as student data grow, and that fixed representations reduce risk only beyond a sample-size threshold. Calibration corrects probability scale but cannot remove excess risk when the teacher coefficient has the wrong direction. In an analysis of 231,521 credit-card complaints, a student trained on teacher probabilities had the same decision cost as the teacher, while one trained on outcomes performed 8% better.
english.practicalApplication: The findings suggest that decision-makers using predicted probabilities should validate teacher-induced bias against realized outcomes rather than relying on calibration or pretrained representations alone. The abstract does not establish direct applications to trading or rates work.
english.methodology: The paper analyzes each training ingredient using Gaussian surrogates with exactly calculable finite-sample risk, studies recalibration in a probit model, derives a coherence condition under Luce's choice axiom, and compares models on U.S. Consumer Financial Protection Bureau credit-card complaint data.
english.limitations: The main theoretical analysis relies on Gaussian surrogates, and the empirical example is limited to a binary decision on credit-card complaints. From the abstract alone, estimation uncertainty, details of the comparison setup, and generalizability to other data or operational settings cannot be assessed.
english.reason: This is research on machine-learning calibration and decision-making, with no demonstrated direct connection to the specified quantitative-finance areas, so it is classified as out of scope.
